Degree lane, the meromorphic bridge W1–W4 COMPLETE (Fable-authored): every Čech Picard class of the integral curve is a divisor class, and equal divisor classes differ by a principal divisor. W1 — sections embed in the function field by germ-at-η (injective on units), and every class L has a meromorphic presentation: elements f_x := germ_η of the cocycle pair values at the canonical base index η, with f_x/f_y = the cocycle on the nose in K(X)ˣ. W2 — the divisor of a presentation, D_x := ord_x(f_x), piece-independent (unit sections have trivial order) with finite support (per-piece principal-divisor finiteness + a finite subcover). W3, the heart — equal presentation divisors give equal classes: on a common refinement the element ratios have matching orders everywhere, the ord-matching lemma turns them into unit sections (via the D=0 divisor sheaf both ways), and the coboundary is checked INSIDE K(X)ˣ by germ injectivity — no sheaf gluing anywhere, per the worksheet's D1 invariant. W4 — extraction: equal classes give cobounding units gluing to one element g of K(X)ˣ with D − D' = div(g); full kernel description picClass_eq_iff. Endpoints: realization of every divisor, the anchored total class map CurveDivisor.picClass with additivity, picClass(div g) = 1, surjectivity (S) and extraction (X) — the degree map's substrate. AUDIT FINDING against deg-D1: the landed pointDivisor seals its equation behind a private postcondition too weak to pin the divisor (s = 1 satisfies it), so the intended statements are formally unprovable against it — the point construction is rebuilt here with the specification public (PointUniformizerData tracking germ_η s = uniformizer), and the one-patch repair recipe to collapse divisorClass into the anchored map is recorded.
